slides.title: RoboScience Unveils Visics, a General-Purpose Embodied AI Model
slides.highlight: The introduction of Visics, a general-purpose embodied AI model, is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated learning.

slides.title: Uncovering Salience-Driven Dynamics in Consumer Confidence with Generative Social Simulation
slides.tldr: GENERATIVE SOCIAL SIMULATION FOR CONSUMER CONFIDENCE
slides.highlight: This work introduces ConsumerSim, a generative framework that reconstructs Consumer Confidence Index dynamics using synthetic populations and behavioral signals, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and agent models.

card.one_liner: ConsumerSim reconstructs Consumer Confidence Index dynamics by simulating heterogeneous household responses to salient environmental signals.
card.key_idea: A generative framework using microdata-calibrated synthetic populations, situational signal fields, post-stratified belief expansion, and behavioral inertia alignment to model CCI as a Human–Environment response process.
card.evaluation: Tested on U.S., EU27, and Japan CCI series against 14 baselines; outperformed others in MAE/RMSE and improved short-horizon housing activity predictions.
card.limitation: Relies on external signal quality, uses generative agents as imperfect cognitive proxies, and lacks full local population substrates for non-U.S. regions.

slides.title: Boundary Degree as a Node-level Feature for Epidemic Scenario Identification in Agent-based Cascade Simulations
slides.tldr: IMPROVING EPIDEMIC SCENARIO IDENTIFICATION VIA BOUNDARY DEGREE
slides.highlight: This research introduces boundary degree as a per-node feature to improve the identification of epidemic scenarios in agent-based simulations, supporting MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis.

card.one_liner: Boundary degree as a per-node feature improves epidemic scenario identification accuracy by an average of 19%.
card.key_idea: The authors propose 'boundary degree'—the count of an infected node's non-infected contacts—as a per-node feature for GNN-based classification of epidemic cascades.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using GNNs on realistic Tennessee/Virginia contact networks and SBM graphs; outperformed feature engineering baselines with >90% accuracy at 20% coverage.
card.limitation: Certain scenario pairs are theoretically indistinguishable without boundary or edge information, limiting learnability in specific cases.

slides.title: REPAIR-Bench: A Benchmark for Robot Error Perception And Interaction Recovery
slides.tldr: BENCHMARK FOR ROBOT FAILURE PERCEPTION AND RECOVERY
slides.highlight: This benchmark provides a framework for evaluating how users perceive robot failures and predicting preferred recovery strategies, supporting the development of trustworthy human-robot interaction for RwB.

card.one_liner: REPAIR-Bench is a multimodal benchmark for detecting, classifying, and predicting recovery strategies for robot interaction failures.
card.key_idea: It uses Hierarchical Recurrent Neural Networks (HRNN) for temporal failure detection/classification and QLoRA-tuned Small Language Models (Mistral-7B, Gemma-9B) to predict user-preferred recovery strategies from transcripts.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 184 samples from 41 participants using F1-scores, Hit@k, and localization error; HRNN achieved 0.80 strict F1 for detection.
card.limitation: Small sample size for recovery prediction (184) and reliance on a predefined set of recovery strategies.

slides.title: Understanding LLM Intervention Explanations in Multi-Party Human-Robot Interaction
slides.highlight: This research examines how LLM-based orchestrators justify decisions to intervene in multi-party human-robot interactions, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: Analysis of LLM-driven robot interventions in multi-party settings reveals a strong bias toward group facilitation.
card.key_idea: An LLM orchestrator managed two robots (mover/opposer) in human group discussions, generating textual justifications for its decisions to intervene or remain silent.
card.evaluation: Thematic analysis of 610 explanations from 24 groups (66 students) using a between-subjects design (homogeneous vs. heterogeneous roles).
card.limitation: Did not evaluate if users understood the explanations or link interventions to objective task success rates.

slides.title: Vision-Language Models for Deployable Social Robot Navigation: Bridging Semantic Reasoning and Low-Level Control
slides.highlight: This survey explores integrating Vision-Language Models with low-level control to enable socially compliant robot navigation, supporting RwB's focus on embodied social robots.

card.one_liner: A survey proposing a hierarchical framework to integrate Vision-Language Models into socially compliant robot navigation systems.
card.key_idea: A three-part architecture coupling high-level VLM semantic reasoning, a bridging mechanism for translation, and low-level planning for safe, real-time control.
card.evaluation: The paper reviews existing SRN datasets and platforms, organizing current VLM-based approaches into five paradigms based on their integration interface.
card.limitation: High computational costs and inference latency of VLMs hinder real-time deployment on resource-constrained mobile robots.

slides.title: Richtech Robotics Launches 24/7 Interactive Streaming Platform Featuring ADAM Humanoid Robot
slides.highlight: Richtech Robotics has launched a 24/7 interactive streaming platform centered on its AI-powered humanoid robot, ADAM. This development is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Who Plays Which Role When? Communication Role Dynamics for Peer Recognition and Team Performance Prediction
slides.tldr: COMMUNICATION ROLE DYNAMICS FOR TEAM PERFORMANCE
slides.highlight: This work operationalizes a taxonomy of communication roles to characterize role dynamics and predict team performance, contributing to HyECHO's goals of modeling hybrid team states and engagement.

card.one_liner: Theory-grounded communication roles predicted by LLMs improve the prediction of peer recognition and team performance.
card.key_idea: Operationalized a taxonomy of eight communication roles using LLMs to annotate longitudinal Slack data, analyzing role dynamics and their predictive utility for collaboration quality.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on student Slack messages and the DeliData corpus using ROC-AUC; role-based features outperformed lexical, conversational, and zero-shot LLM baselines.
card.limitation: Primary data from a single CS course may limit generalizability; potential for selection bias and LLM language-style biases.

slides.title: Charting the Growth of Social-Physical HRI (spHRI): A Systematic Review Pipeline Augmented by Small Language Models
slides.highlight: This research evaluates using small language models to accelerate the screening of social-physical human-robot interaction literature, supporting the development of embodied social robots for RwB.

card.one_liner: Small Language Models (SLMs) can augment systematic reviews by recovering relevant papers missed by human reviewers.
card.key_idea: A pipeline using a unanimity ensemble of four locally deployed SLMs (≤1.5B parameters) as a second-pass filter for title and abstract screening in spHRI research.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on 32,000 records; SLM ensemble identified 39 missed relevant papers (10.29% of final set), though individual SLMs performed worse than humans.
card.limitation: SLMs provide binary outputs without confidence scores and cannot yet replace expert judgment due to precision-recall tradeoffs.

slides.title: Metric Aggregation Divergence: A Hidden Validity Threat in Agent-Based Policy Optimization and a Contractual Remedy
slides.tldr: REMEDY FOR METRIC AGGREGATION DIVERGENCE IN ABM+MOEA
slides.highlight: This research identifies metric aggregation divergence in agent-based models coupled with multi-objective evolutionary algorithms and proposes a 'metric contract' to ensure consistency. This is relevant to MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and impact analysis of hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Metric Aggregation Divergence (MAD) causes silent policy recommendation errors when pipeline stages independently implement outcome metrics.
card.key_idea: MAD occurs when different pipeline stages use incommensurable aggregators (e.g., mean vs. entropy). The authors propose a 'metric contract'—a single shared callable enforced across all stages.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via controlled experiments on 4 ABMs and audits of published toolboxes (EpidemiOptim, Lake Problem), showing champion disagreement rates up to 83%.
card.limitation: Tested on only two policy domains (ecology, epidemiology); generalizability to other domains like transportation or energy remains open.

slides.title: SupplyNet: Supporting Visual Exploratory Learning in Supply Chain via Contextual Multi-Agent Simulation
slides.tldr: VISUAL LLM-DRIVEN MULTI-AGENT SUPPLY CHAIN SIMULATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a contextual graph-based LLM multi-agent framework for simulating interdependent supply chain dynamics, aligning with MIMIC's focus on societal-scale simulation and LLM-based agent models.

card.one_liner: SupplyNet is a gamified visual simulation system for learning supply chain dynamics via LLM-driven multi-agent simulation.
card.key_idea: Combines a contextual graph-based LLM multi-agent framework with a branching timeline for "what-if" exploration, an interactive network view, and a task-oriented analysis console.
card.evaluation: A user study comparing SupplyNet to a classic baseline simulation showed increased engagement and improved perceived understanding of supply chain dynamics.

slides.title: NavIsaacLab: Generating Realistic Crowd via Parallel Robot Learning for Benchmarking Human-aware Navigation
slides.highlight: NavIsaacLab provides a physics-based, photo-realistic simulation framework for training and benchmarking human-aware navigation policies, supporting RwB's focus on human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: NavIsaacLab is a GPU-parallelized simulation framework for benchmarking and training human-aware robot navigation policies.
card.key_idea: Combines a trajectory diffusion model with an adversarial motion learning (AMP) controller to generate physics-based, photorealistic, and controllable pedestrian behaviors within Isaac Lab.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via 30 photorealistic scenes; compared against SFM and IsaacSim animations using success rates, pose entropy, and Motion-MMD metrics.
card.limitation: Some challenging locomotion transitions and long-tail motions remain difficult to reproduce accurately.

slides.title: GROVE: Grounded Pedestrian Simulation via Natural Language for Interactive Social Robot Navigation
slides.highlight: GROVE enables the generation of realistic, socially challenging pedestrian scenarios via natural language to improve social robot navigation. This supports RwB by providing high-fidelity simulations to narrow the sim2real gap for robots in social environments.

card.one_liner: GROVE is a text-to-scenario framework that generates realistic, grounded pedestrian simulations for social robot navigation training.
card.key_idea: Combines LLMs with RAG for behavior tree generation, Theta* for global planning, and Social Force Models for local interaction across three behavioral horizons.
card.evaluation: Qualitative trajectory analysis and VLM-based scoring (GPT-5) against Text-Crowd and TRACE baselines in hospital, office, and residential environments.
card.limitation: High computational inference costs and a reliance on static obstacle maps, ignoring dynamic environmental changes.

slides.title: SICAGE: Speaker-Independent Culture-Aware Gesture Generation using TED4C-L Dataset
slides.highlight: SICAGE introduces a framework for generating culturally appropriate gestures that are independent of speaker identity. This is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and understanding group norms in human-AI interaction.

card.one_liner: SICAGE generates culture-aware co-speech gestures using speaker-independent embeddings to avoid confounding individual style with cultural patterns.
card.key_idea: A modular framework using Fishr regularization or adversarial learning to extract speaker-invariant cultural embeddings from audio/text, conditioning a real-time diffusion generator (ALaDiT).
card.evaluation: Evaluated on the new TED4C-L dataset (106h, 4 cultures) using FGD, BAS, SRGR, and a user study with 20 participants.
card.limitation: The model uses only 9 upper-body keypoints, omitting finger and lower-body motion due to detection noise in unconstrained videos.
